optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Data Product Analyst, Low-Code Application Platform
professionalSummary: Experienced analyst with a proven track record in defining, maintaining, and communicating key platform metrics for a low‑code application environment. Demonstrated ability to investigate anomalies, coordinate cross‑functional changes, and present findings to both product management and customer‑facing teams.
experienceHighlights: Defined weekly active builders, app publish rate, and app error‑rate metrics in the analytics warehouse using dbt on BigQuery and maintained a comprehensive metric definitions page.
Investigated a significant April drop in app publish rate, identified a permission change in the publishing service, and documented the root cause and fix in the analytics incident log.
Presented monthly findings to product management and quarterly findings to the customer success team using a structured deck that highlighted trends, causes, and recommended actions.
Coordinated metric definition changes with platform and data engineering teams through the formal data change process, clearly recording ownership boundaries.
Managed all aspects of metric definition, anomaly investigation, stakeholder communication, and change coordination for the low‑code platform over approximately two years.
projectsAndWorkSamples: Metric definitions page export and April anomaly investigation write‑up (timeline, cause, fix, verification query) with warehouse query history as verification trail.
optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The provided resume and work samples establish the candidate’s experience in metric definition, anomaly investigation, stakeholder presentation, and coordination with platform and data engineering teams. They do not provide evidence of the candidate’s ability to document metric definitions, known limitations, and hand‑over conditions for each change, nor do they confirm the candidate’s experience with the analytics incident log beyond the April anomaly.

decisionBoundary.statement: The evidence supports all listed requirements except for documentation of metric definitions, known limitations, and hand‑over conditions for each change.

role.roleTitle: Data Product Analyst, Low-Code Application Platform

evidence.text: Defined the platform's weekly active builders, app publish rate and app error-rate metrics in the analytics warehouse (dbt models on BigQuery) and maintained the metric definitions page.
evidence.notes: Directly matches metric definition and maintenance

evidence.text: Responsibilities included metric definition, anomaly investigation, stakeholder presentations and change coordination for the low-code platform over about two years.
Investigated the April drop in app publish rate with the platform team, traced it to a permission change in the publishing service and documented the cause and the fix in the analytics incident log.

Interviewer 1 note: when asked to explain the April anomaly, the candidate gave the timeline in order, named the permission change as the cause, said which team fixed it and how the fix was verified, and checked whether the non-technical interviewer had followed before moving on.
Presented monthly findings to product management and quarterly findings to the customer success team, using a standard deck with metric trend, cause and recommended follow-up for each anomaly.
Reference call with former product manager: confirmed the candidate presented monthly to product management, that the April investigation was the candidate's, and confirmed the employment dates.

Coordinated metric definition changes with the platform and data engineering teams through the data change process, recording my ownership of the definitions and data engineering's ownership of the pipelines.
